prompt: A researcher randomly selected $200$ students from Lincoln High School and found that $62\%$ preferred a later start time. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.label: About $62\%$ of all high school students nationwide prefer a later start time
About $62\%$ of students at Lincoln High School prefer a later start time
A later start time causes students to perform better
Exactly $62\%$ of students at Lincoln High School prefer a later start time

hint: A sample can only speak for the population it was drawn from.

hints.text: A sample can only speak for the population it was drawn from.
The sample came from one school, so the conclusion covers that school.
About $62\%$ of Lincoln High School students — an estimate, not an exact figure.

learningObjective: Determine the population a random sample supports conclusions about.
explanation: The students were randomly selected from Lincoln High School, so that school is the population the sample represents.
Choice A over-generalizes to a population never sampled. Choice C claims causation, which requires a controlled experiment with random assignment.
Choice D says "exactly", but a sample gives an estimate with uncertainty, not an exact population value. Choice B — "about", and scoped to the right population — is correct.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two questions settle every inference item
steps: First: who was sampled? The conclusion may not extend beyond that group.
Second: was there random *assignment* to treatments? Without it you cannot claim cause.
Random selection buys generalization; random assignment buys causation. They are different, and no study gets one for free from the other.
